title: Which Housing Feature Does the Job?
description: Classify twelve job-site requests by the housing feature or opening accessory that meets each one, choosing from four options per request, with hints after a first wrong try, a summary of every request and a Retry missed practice round.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: welded housing
bolted housing

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
learningObjectives: The learner will classify 12 job-site requests by the housing feature or opening accessory that meets each one, choosing from four options per request.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts, each new request and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); options are native buttons; keys 1-4 choose, Enter goes to the next request; ✓/✗ glyphs with solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the summary list is a focusable, scrollable region.

controls.label: Options 1-4
controls.purpose: Commit an option for the current request (keys 1-4)

controls.label: Next request / See summary
controls.purpose: Advance after a request is resolved (Enter)

controls.label: Retry missed
controls.purpose: Practice round over the missed requests (not scored)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reset all twelve requests and the score

rules: Twelve requests in a fixed order, four options each in the listed order, one correct option per request.
Two attempts; a wrong first try shows a hint naming the job of the correct feature; a second miss reveals the answer with its Why text.
Mastery: 10 of 12 on the first attempt.

sources: FanPedia, pages 7, 8, 18, 19, 59, 117, 120, 125, 156, 157, 180, 181 and 194 (feature definitions, through this chapter's sections)
Requests are illustrative job-site wording written for this chapter

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification with near-miss distractors that share a location or a word with the right answer
keyQuestions: What is the difference between a bird screen and a safety screen?
When does a backdraft damper act?
commonMisconceptions: Bird screens and safety screens are interchangeable.
An inspection port allows cleaning and impeller removal (it allows viewing only).
A collar and a flange are the same connection.
A backdraft damper controls airflow while the fan runs (it only stops reverse flow when the fan is off).
A split housing is only for maintenance (it is also used for shipping and tight openings).
assessmentOpportunities: 'Requests correct: n of 12' running score; the summary shows the first-attempt score; mastery is 10 of 12 on the first attempt.
